prediction_fields.name: federal_enforcement_budget_usd
prediction_fields.description: Federal resources allocated during calendar year 2022 to No Surprises Act oversight, complaint handling, audits, and enforcement.

prediction_fields.name: certified_idr_entity_count
prediction_fields.description: Number of certified independent dispute resolution entities active and available to accept federal IDR cases during calendar year 2022.

prediction_fields.name: qpa_ready_plan_pct
prediction_fields.description: Percentage of group health plans and health insurance issuers with operational data and systems to calculate the Qualifying Payment Amount accurately at the start of 2022.

discussion_points: Where are enforcement resources insufficient for complaint processing, auditing, or corrective action?
Does certified IDR capacity match the expected volume and geographic distribution of payment disputes?
Which data, contracting, or system limitations prevent plans from calculating reliable QPAs?

prediction_fields.name: qpa_calculations_completed
prediction_fields.description: Number of QPA calculations completed by plans and issuers during 2022 for protected out-of-network claims subject to the No Surprises Act.

prediction_fields.name: timely_initial_payment_or_denial_rate
prediction_fields.description: Percentage of eligible protected claims in 2022 for which a plan or issuer issued an initial payment or denial notice within the applicable 30-day window.

prediction_fields.name: idr_cases_initiated
prediction_fields.description: Number of federal IDR payment disputes initiated during calendar year 2022 after open negotiation did not resolve the payment amount.

discussion_points: How do inaccurate or disputed QPA calculations propagate into payment negotiation and IDR demand?
Which operational constraints cause late initial payments or denial notices?
Under what conditions do negotiations break down and move into IDR, including high-cost or specialized services?

prediction_fields.name: protected_claims_correctly_processed_rate
prediction_fields.description: Percentage of NSA-protected out-of-network claims processed during 2022 with the correct in-network patient cost-sharing and applicable payment procedure.

prediction_fields.name: notice_compliance_rate
prediction_fields.description: Percentage of 2022 encounters subject to NSA disclosure requirements in which the required notice was complete, timely, and correctly provided.

prediction_fields.name: timely_idr_determination_rate
prediction_fields.description: Percentage of federal IDR cases decided during 2022 within the applicable administrative determination timeline.

discussion_points: What processing failures still expose protected patients to incorrect out-of-network cost sharing or balance bills?
When does notice-and-consent implementation fail to provide meaningful and informed patient choice?
How do IDR delays affect provider cash flow, plan administration, and willingness to negotiate?

prediction_fields.name: emergency_oon_bill_prevalence_reduction_pp
prediction_fields.description: Percentage-point reduction in the prevalence of out-of-network bills for emergency services in 2022 relative to the pre-NSA baseline.

prediction_fields.name: nonemergency_oon_bill_prevalence_reduction_pp
prediction_fields.description: Percentage-point reduction in the prevalence of out-of-network bills for non-emergency services delivered at in-network facilities in 2022 relative to the pre-NSA baseline.

prediction_fields.name: patient_savings_per_protected_claim_usd
prediction_fields.description: Average reduction in patient out-of-pocket liability per NSA-protected out-of-network claim in 2022 relative to the amount expected under pre-NSA billing rules.

discussion_points: Which service types, specialties, patient groups, or locations experience smaller reductions or continuing surprise bills?
Are notice-and-consent waivers, claim reclassification, or other substitution effects offsetting the observed reductions?
How are savings distributed across emergency and non-emergency claims, and which patients remain financially exposed?

prediction_fields.name: systemic_oon_billing_prevalence_pct
prediction_fields.description: National prevalence of out-of-network balance billing among services covered by the No Surprises Act three to five years after implementation.

prediction_fields.name: network_adequacy_rate_pct
prediction_fields.description: Percentage of regulated health plans meeting applicable network adequacy standards three to five years after NSA implementation.

prediction_fields.name: premium_change_attributable_to_nsa_pct
prediction_fields.description: Estimated percentage change in health plan premiums three to five years after implementation that is attributable to NSA compliance, contracting, and payment effects.

discussion_points: Do contracting responses and provider or plan consolidation produce durable reductions in surprise billing or shift costs elsewhere?
Does the policy preserve adequate access to emergency, specialty, air ambulance, and rural services?
How do payment and compliance costs affect premiums, provider participation, and long-term market behavior?
Which unintended consequences would indicate that short-term consumer protection did not translate into durable system-level improvement?
